notes: A chronic, major SI4 pressure the pollution cluster (focused on agriculture and sewage) never queried. It explains a significant share of why only 40 percent of Welsh water bodies reach good status, the SoNaRR baseline the indicator is read against, so it threatens SI4 and informs its baseline. Found via the July 2026 coverage audit; a metal-mine query was added to the pollution cluster.
summary: About 1,300 abandoned metal mines put over 500 tonnes of metals (zinc, lead, cadmium, iron) into Welsh rivers every year, causing roughly 700km, about 6 percent of Welsh rivers, to fail good chemical or ecological status. The Wales Metal Mines Programme (Natural Resources Wales with the Mining Remediation Authority, Welsh Government funded) is remediating priority sites. The House of Commons Welsh Affairs Committee inquiry into metal mine pollution in Wales took oral evidence on 1 July 2026 and on 21 July 2026 wrote to the Secretary of State for Wales calling for four-nation lead testing of children, food testing standards, farmer support and clearer public risk information, with a reply requested by 7 September 2026; the committee pressed again in a letter reported on 15 September 2026, and no government reply had been published by 6 October 2026. The Welsh Government's Programme for Government (22 September 2026) commits to a Wales-wide strategy to map, prioritise and restore contaminated post-industrial land and polluted waterways, while pressing the UK Government to fund it.
title: Abandoned metal mines pollute about 700km of Welsh rivers, a major SI4 pressure with a live inquiry
